Appeals Court Sides With Ohio, Tennessee

The 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Cincinnati unanimously rejected Kalshi’s argument that its sports contracts are financial "swaps" subject exclusively to federal oversight by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission or CFTC.
The court also found that federal commodities law does not prevent Ohio and Tennessee from enforcing their gambling regulations.
Judge Julia
Smith Gibbons
wrote that contracts tied to outcomes such as soccer corner kicks do not clearly serve the financial risk-management purposes associated with derivatives regulated under federal commodities law.

children: Kalshi Warns of Regulatory Patchwork
The ruling vacated a preliminary injunction previously issued against Tennessee and upheld a similar denial in Ohio, Reuters reported.
Kalshi said the decision highlights why nationwide federal regulation is needed.
"The ruling shows exactly why" a state-by-state approach does not work, spokesperson
Dani Lever
said, arguing that prediction markets cannot operate effectively when rules differ across state lines.
Kalshi did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment.
Prediction markets allow users to trade contracts tied to events ranging from sports and elections to weather and entertainment.
